descriptions: The log prints state->K using "%s" even though the copied key is length-delimited (params[0].memref.size) and not validated/forced to be NUL-terminated. This can cause an out-of-bounds read past the key bytes within state->K until a NUL is encountered, leaking adjacent memory via logging.

The log prints state->K using %s, which treats the buffer as NUL-terminated string; since the copied key length is REE-controlled and not validated/forced to include a terminator, the print may read past the intended key length (out-of-bounds read) until a NUL is encountered.
why_not_categories: Not Direct Usage of Shared Memory: the read is from trusted-private state->K, not directly from shared memory.
Not Unencrypted Data Output: the core issue is an out-of-bounds read due to treating binary data as a C-string, not copying a secret into shared memory.
Not other: fits Input Validation Weakness as a missing content/termination validation leading to unsafe read.
Not Direct Usage of Shared Memory: the read is from trusted state->K, not directly from a shared-memory alias at this point.
Not Unencrypted Data Output: although it may leak key material via logs, it is not a copy to untrusted-visible shared memory as defined by UDO.
Not other: the core issue is missing validation/termination for a length-controlled string read.
code_snippets: DMSG("Got shared key %s (%u bytes).", state->K, params[0].memref.size);
